transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I keep having these evenings where I just eat a really large amount of food. I'll buy a whole family-size takeout order, and then I usually add chips or bakery things from the store on the way home. And I just eat most of it myself before I even seem to register how much is actually gone.
When you're eating all of that food, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating or that you're not in control of yourself during those times?

Yes, that's exactly how it feels. It's like... once I start eating, there is this awful switch that flips. I can literally be sitting there thinking to myself, 'Taylor, just put it away,' but my hands still keep opening the containers anyway. It really feels like I am not the one in charge anymore.
After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you ever try to compensate for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do any of that. I just... I feel terrible about it afterward, but I don't try to throw up or take anything. And I'm definitely not exercising it off. I just sit with it.
How often do these episodes happen, and do they cause you a lot of emotional distress afterward?

Well, I actually keep a journal, and... when I look back through it, there has barely been a week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks it happens several times. 

And yes, it causes a lot of distress. I feel incredibly upset and ashamed of myself every time it happens.

latest_inference.note: The patient does not engage in compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise, which rules out F50.02 (Bulimia Nervosa). F50.00 (Anorexia Nervosa) is also ruled out as there is no evidence of restrictive eating or fear of weight gain. The presentation is consistent with F50.01 (Binge Eating Disorder).
